finding: The previous reserve implementation displayed six simultaneous 100,000-contract base quotes, increasing with depth. Large funded capital should instead support modest displayed quotes replenished over time.

sources.title: CME: COMEX Gold Futures and Options, APAC Liquidity
sources.limitation: Historical illustration; not a current depth target for every market or session.

sources.title: CME: Reassessing Liquidity Beyond Order Book Depth
sources.finding: Depth, traded volume and execution impact are different measures. Replenishment and fill quality matter alongside a resting snapshot.

sources.title: CME Liquidity Tool
sources.finding: Depth and execution cost must be evaluated by product, time window and order size. Authenticated current datasets were not accessed.

sources.title: CME: Hidden Quantity order functionality
sources.finding: Documented futures support for displaying part of a larger order and refreshing the displayed part after execution.
sources.limitation: Historical functionality reference. This implementation submits new finite quotes; it does not implement native exchange iceberg order semantics.

implementation.capitalAndInventory: Existing funded reserve balances and inventory retained; only actual submitted child quotes appear in depth.
implementation.migration: Withdraw obsolete reserve quotes, retain positions and account balances, schedule modest replacements without trading during restore.
implementation.fairness: Divide each market's execution allowance among waiting owners before applying per-owner and depth limits.

limits: These are simulation calibration choices, not measured current CME averages.
Displayed levels aggregate many participants; uneven levels and occasional large orders can be legitimate.
Large player limit orders remain genuine visible orders; this change targets artificial bot walls, not falsifying the depth display.
Realistic displayed depth means large parent orders may remain queued much longer. Billion-dollar balances do not guarantee immediate execution.
CapacityTests intentionally use an oversized synthetic liquidity fixture to test arithmetic and queue ceilings; they do not measure the new production fill speed.
